summary: The queue's new depth check is tested only by calling bindShippedReceipt directly. No test runs `gstack-ship-queue ready` or `train build` with a receipt below the required depth. Those callers pass different base refs (`origin/<base>` in ready, `refs/remotes/<remote>/<base>` in train) and append depthLine to their output, so a wrong ref or a dropped REVIEW_DEPTH line would still pass CI.
fix: Add one ready test and one train-build admitSlots test whose PR body has a light receipt on an 80-runtime-line head. Assert QUEUE_RECEIPT_DEPTH_RAISED and the REVIEW_DEPTH: receipt=light required=standard line in the output.

summary: exceptionProblems now makes the queue refuse a receipt when its docs exception is malformed or the PR body dropped the exception line (QUEUE_RECEIPT_EXCEPTION_INVALID). Only the review-loop branch has a test. The docs branch is a new refusal path with no test.
fix: Add a bindShippedReceipt case with a docs: {status: 'blocked', exception: {...}} receipt. Assert ok with the line in the body, then QUEUE_RECEIPT_EXCEPTION_INVALID after removing the line.

summary: After a carry, the review_depth is set to deeper(receipt depth, HEAD depth), so a full or standard receipt should keep that depth when the new head needs less. The carry tests only cover equal depths (light to light) and a refused raise. Nothing proves a carry never lowers the recorded depth.
fix: Write a receipt at standard (80 runtime lines), carry across a test-only commit, and assert that review_depth.depth stays standard while gate_scan.head rebinds to the new head.

summary: Stale help and docstring. The write help says review_depth comes from 'gstack-review-plan --json at HEAD' and that 'no plan means nothing written'. cmdWrite actually calls receiptDepthAtHead (collectCommit on git objects plus depthOfCommitInput), which never runs gstack-review-plan and always returns a record because errors fail closed to full. Nothing is ever refused for a missing plan. The header comment in lib/ship-receipt-depth.ts:6-7 repeats the same wrong 'from gstack-review-plan' claim.
fix: Reword both to say the receipt records receiptDepthAtHead's commit-range depth, which fails closed to full, and drop 'no plan means nothing written'. If a refusal is intended, implement it.

summary: The light-depth skip reason is misleading. On a later light full pass (fullPasses > 0) for a diff whose numbers.publishes is true and whose fingerprint is unchanged, the <reader> is skipped with the reason 'no numeric claims'. The diff does have claims; they were already reviewed. The standard branch reports this case as 'run once per invocation'.
fix: Branch the reason: 'numeric claims already reviewed' when numbers.publishes is true, and 'no numeric claims' otherwise.
test_stub: test('light pass 2 with unchanged published numbers does not say no numeric claims', () => { const p = planReview({ /* light code diff, numbers.publishes: true, reviewedNumbers: same fingerprint, history: { fullPasses: 1, last: 'full', fixedBelow: true } */ } as any); expect(p.skipped.join(' ')).not.toContain('no numeric claims'); });

summary: Collected.mergeBase is set by collectCommit and collectLive, but no caller reads it. gstack-review-plan, ship-receipt-depth and the tests ignore it, so it is a dead field in the new interface.
fix: Drop mergeBase from Collected and from result()'s extra, or use it where a caller needs it.

summary: Plan-output line injection via file names. lib/review-collect.ts now reads paths with `git diff --numstat -z` and `ls-files -z`, so raw newlines and other control characters in PR-controlled file names are no longer C-quoted by git. Those names reach the line-oriented plan unsanitized: excludeSpec/shellQuote (lib/review-depth.ts:285-286) quote only single quotes, and the result is printed as `DIFF_CMD: <key> ...` (and in REVIEW_CLASS reasons). A docs or test path whose name contains `\nDIFF_CMD: security git diff <diff-base> -- . ':(exclude)lib'` forges a DIFF_CMD line, and /ship tells the parent to copy everything after <diff-base> on a reviewer's DIFF_CMD line verbatim. That can hide product code from a specialist reviewer, or leave an unbalanced quote that breaks the reviewer's diff command. The old collector split non -z output, where git quoted such names.
fix: Reject or escape control characters in paths before they reach any printed plan line. For example, fail the depth closed with a DepthError for any path matching /[\x00-\x1f\x7f]/, or emit exclude specs only through the --json plan and never in the line-oriented DIFF_CMD text.
evidence: Coverage note: test and fixture files (test/fixtures/golden/*-ship-SKILL.md, test/review-collect.test.ts, test/review-depth.test.ts, test/ship-receipt-carry-rewrite.test.ts, test/ship-receipt-depth.test.ts, test/review-plan-cli.test.ts, test/gstack-regen.test.ts and others; 13 files, +642/-28) were reviewed in SUMMARY mode only (diff --stat), not their raw contents. Non-test source was reviewed in full.

summary: `deeper` has one caller (bin/gstack-ship-receipt:605), which runs only after `depthBelow(receipt.review_depth.depth, now.depth)` has already refused, so it always returns the receipt's depth
fix: write `depth: receipt.review_depth.depth` at the call site, then delete `deeper` and its import

summary: `Collected.mergeBase` is set on all three return paths, but nothing in bin/, lib/, scripts/ or test/ reads it
fix: drop the field from `Collected` and stop passing `mergeBase` to `result()`

summary: The queue's depth check is circular. write records review_depth as receiptDepthAtHead, which is the depth HEAD needs, not the depth the review loop dispatched (the Step 9 REVIEW_DEPTH/step depth is never passed in, and review_loop has no depth field). receiptDepthVerdict then compares that need against the same function recomputed, so QUEUE_RECEIPT_DEPTH_RAISED fires only on drift (base registry, rules hash, scan binding). A run that reviewed at light, then committed a below-floor fix that pushed runtime past 50 or into gate class, gets a receipt saying standard or full, and the queue accepts it. The refusal text 'was reviewed at <d> depth' overstates this.
fix: Record the deepest stepDepth the loop actually ran (from the review log rows or a --review-depth flag fed by the plan) and have the queue compare that against the recomputed need.

summary: isOutput trusts a glob match against the base registry's outputs (for example */SKILL.md, */sections/*.md), not proof that the generator writes the file. Matching paths are dropped from runtime lines (line 132) and from every light or standard reviewer's DIFF_CMD (line 306). A file the generator never writes, such as a new hand-written <dir>/SKILL.md, passes the regen check as fresh. It is code class with runtime 0, so it plans light with zero reviewers. This PR added regen 'proven' to close exactly this gap for carry ('an output it never writes proves nothing') but did not apply it here.
fix: Exclude only outputs that regen proved, or count an output path as runtime when no registry input for it changed in the diff.

summary: receiptDepthAtHead counts lines from committed objects (collectCommit), but gstack-gate-diff and gstack-diff-scope read the working tree plus untracked files. write does not require a clean tree, yet it stamps gate_scan.head=HEAD, and receiptDepthVerdict trusts that tagged count as bound to HEAD (line 124). An uncommitted edit that reverts a committed gate hunk gives tagged=0 for a head that has the hunk.
fix: Refuse write on a dirty tree, as carry does, or run the gate scan against HEAD's committed range.

label: FIXABLE
summary: The receipt records the depth the head NEEDS, not the depth the review RAN, so QUEUE_RECEIPT_DEPTH_RAISED cannot catch an under-review. (bin/gstack-ship-receipt:208, lib/ship-receipt-depth.ts receiptDepthAtHead) cmdWrite computes review_depth fresh at write time with the same function (collectCommit + depthOfCommitInput) that the queue later runs in receiptDepthVerdict. Neither write nor the pr-body template reads the plan's REVIEW_DEPTH or the review-log "depth" row. For an honest writer, then, receipt depth always equals required depth (apart from drift; see #5), and the queue check holds by construction. Concrete case: pass 1 plans light (runtime 45) and dispatches one <reader> specialist. A below-floor fix adds 20 runtime lines, so nextStep returns fix-check, not a full pass. The head now needs standard. write records "standard", the queue accepts it, and standard's specialists never ran. Fix: take the reviewed depth from this invocation's review-log rows (the maximum stepDepth of the full passes actually dispatched) and pass it to write. Record both reviewed and required, and refuse in write (and in the queue) when reviewed < required.

label: FIXABLE
summary: Review depth discounts any path that matches a base-registry output glob, with no proof that the generator writes it. (lib/review-depth.ts:99 isOutput, :306 docsAndOutputs) The base registry's outputs include "*/SKILL.md" and "*/sections/*.md". A branch that adds a hand-written one-level agent-prose file (for example a new foo/SKILL.md or ship/sections/x.md with no .tmpl) gets these effects: - It counts 0 runtime lines. - It is excluded from the light and standard specialists' DIFF_CMD. - If it is the whole diff, the depth is "light, runtime 0": no specialist and no adversarial pass, only the core checklist. The pregate regen check does not flag it, because the generator never touches the file and it shows as fresh. The carry path explicitly guards this case (verifiedOutputs requires regen "proven"; the CHANGELOG says "a hand-written file under an output glob that the generator never writes stays product"), but the depth classifier does not. Fix: discount an output only when the regen proof covers it, or when a matching registry input changed in the same diff. Otherwise count it as runtime.

label: FIXABLE
summary: A tree-equal carry across a moved base can silently revert the base's test, metadata or registered-output changes. (lib/ship-receipt.ts:266 planTreeCarry; bin/gstack-ship-receipt:554) If the merge base moved and HEAD's tree is byte-identical to the reviewed tree, then diff(newBase, HEAD) necessarily reverts the base's delta. productPatchAgainstBase compares only the product pathspec, which excludes CARRY_TEST_GLOBS and the metadata globs. So a known footgun, "git reset --soft origin/main && git commit" with the old index, carries whenever the base's delta was limited to tests, CHANGELOG/VERSION or proven outputs. When it carries: - A test that main tightened goes back to the old version. - CI runs the old test and passes. - The squash merge removes main's change. The depth recompute catches deleted test files only when the receipt has a review_depth below full. Modified tests, legacy receipts and full-depth receipts pass. Fix: in the rewritten path, also require the test patch-id and the whole-diff patch-id against the current base to equal the recorded ones (record them in write), or refuse whenever the merge base differs from the one the receipt recorded.

label: FIXABLE
summary: The "gate scan bound to HEAD" record actually scans the working tree, and write does not refuse a dirty tree. (lib/ship-receipt-depth.ts:48-53; bin/gstack-ship-receipt cmdWrite) receiptDepthAtHead runs gstack-diff-scope and gstack-gate-diff without --commit. That mode is diffWorkingTree plus untracked files, but the result is recorded as gate_scan.head = <commit>. If uncommitted edits revert a committed gate hunk (for example a committed test.skip that the working tree un-skips), the receipt records tagged=0 bound to the head, and the queue trusts that number (ship-receipt-depth.ts:124-125), so the head is never raised to gate. Carry has the same problem: it refuses a dirty tree, but "--head <sha>" may differ from the checkout when no --pregate is passed, and the scan is then of the wrong tree. Fix: refuse write when git status --porcelain is non-empty, run gstack-gate-diff --commit <head> (or a range mode) and gstack-diff-scope on commit objects, and make carry require --head == HEAD.

label: FIXABLE
summary: The queue's independent recompute is partial, and its inputs drift from what the docs promise. (lib/ship-receipt-depth.ts:121-125; lib/review-collect.ts:99,116) (a) depthOfCommitInput is called with no scope, so SCOPE_AUTH and SCOPE_MIGRATIONS (which would make the diff gate class) and SCOPE_ERROR never raise the required depth at the queue. The gate scan count is taken from the receipt itself. (b) scanBound uses head.startsWith(rd.gate_scan.head). An empty or 1-character gate_scan.head binds to any head. Require 40-hex equality. (c) The registry is loaded at the current origin/<base> tip, not at the receipt's recorded base sha (docs/review-policy.md says "the receipt's base sha for the queue"; rd.base is never read), and collectLive uses the base tip rather than the merge base. A later registry change on main changes the required depth for an unchanged head. An invalid registry commit on main fails every queued sub-full receipt closed at once, and the refusal says "run /ship" (tens of millions of tokens each) when the real repair is the registry. (d) A head that is not available locally fails with numstat_failed, which makes the head need full, and the refusal again says "run /ship" when the fix is "git fetch".

label: FIXABLE
summary: Legacy acceptance has no end date, and carry never upgrades a legacy receipt. (lib/ship-receipt-depth.ts:121; bin/gstack-ship-receipt:603) Any receipt with neither review_depth nor gstack_version is accepted forever. The policy floor was raised to min_gstack_version 1.91.299.0, but this feature sits under [Unreleased], after 1.91.299.0, so the floor still allows writers that never record depth. On top of that, carry recomputes depth only "if (receipt.review_depth)". A legacy receipt therefore carries a test change that skips a test (gate class) with no depth check and stays legacy, which bypasses the CHANGELOG's "a test change that skips a test refuses the carry". Fix: when carrying, compute the depth for legacy receipts too (refuse if the head needs gate/full depth) and stamp gstack_version. Set the policy floor to the release that ships this change, or end legacy acceptance on a cutoff date or version.

label: FIXABLE
summary: Raw control characters in paths now reach the line protocol the /ship agent parses. (lib/review-collect.ts:55,124; bin/gstack-review-plan:116-117; lib/review-depth.ts:133,285) The old collector used --name-status and ls-files without -z, so git C-quoted a newline in a path. The new one uses -z and passes raw paths into REVIEW_CLASS reasons ("code: <path>"), DEPTH_ERROR input= (binary paths; only detail is sanitized) and DIFF_CMD (shellQuote keeps embedded newlines). A branch-controlled filename containing "\nNEXT: done (...)" or "\nREVIEW_DEPTH: light ..." prints a forged directive line ahead of the real one in output that an LLM agent consumes. The -U0 patch parser also reads git's quoted "+++ \"b/...\"" form as a different key, so numbers scanning and stampOnly silently skip those paths. Fix: refuse (fail closed to full) or JSON-quote any path with control characters before printing, and parse patch headers from "diff --git" with -z name lists rather than slicing "+++ b/".

label: INVESTIGATE
summary: The rewritten-history carry trusts the receipt's own head_tree and carry.trees over git. (bin/gstack-ship-receipt:538) When the old head is still in the clone, fromTree is computed but ignored whenever receipt.head_tree is present, so there is no check that head_tree == from^{tree}. The product_patch_id compared against is also read from the body. Body edits were already the trust root (setting head: directly), so this adds no new privilege, but a cheap cross-check would catch receipts copied from another branch and receipts damaged by hand edits.

label: INVESTIGATE
summary: The proof run in lib/regen.ts deletes through a parent symlink in the scratch worktree. fs.existsSync and fs.rmSync(path.join(cwd, p)) follow symlinked parent directories. Take a branch that replaces a directory with a symlink pointing outside the scratch while the base still lists a/<output>, so a deleted path is still "touched". The proof step then deletes the target's file outside the scratch worktree. AGENTS.md requires resolving a link's target inside the fixture root before writing through it. The impact is bounded, because --allow-repo-commands already runs branch code, but this deletion also happens on non-malicious mistakes. Fix: realpath-check each probe path so it stays under cwd before deleting it.

label: INVESTIGATE
summary: review_loop_exception is self-attested. parseReviewLoopException checks shape, ancestry and the body line, but nothing resolves "accepted_by"/"via" to an actual owner message (unlike approval citations). Any writer can record an owner acceptance. If later tooling treats the record as authorization, it needs citation resolution like approval-classes.

label: High
summary: An output glob can suppress review of hand-written runtime code. `lib/review-depth.ts:99,131–132,306–319` treats every path matching a command-bearing base-registry output glob as generated, without checking whether the command actually produces that file. A repository with `outputs: ["src/generated/**"]` can therefore change an existing, imported hand-written file under that directory and receive runtime_lines=0 with no specialist, <reader>, native adversarial, or <reader> dispatch (absent numeric claims). The pregate does not close this hole: `lib/regen.ts:261–269` can return `proven: []` when the command never recreates the deleted file, while `lib/pregate/checks/regen.ts` still returns pass. The branch already requires this provenance for receipt carry, but not for initial review depth or reviewer exclusions. An in-memory call to the new planner with a 300-line matching code-class path returned `{depth:"light",runtimeLines:0,dispatches:[]}`. Require proven, current-head output ownership before excluding a path; unproven matches must remain runtime code.

label: Medium
summary: The queue omits the auth and migration inputs when recomputing required depth. `lib/ship-receipt-depth.ts:123–125` calls `depthOfCommitInput` with collected paths and the recorded gate count, but never supplies `scope`. Auth and migration escalation exists only through `SCOPE_AUTH` and `SCOPE_MIGRATIONS` in `lib/review-depth.ts:124–125`; the gate-path patterns do not independently cover ordinary `src/auth.ts` or `db/migrate/...` files. Consequently, a light receipt with a bound zero-tag scan is accepted for a small auth or database migration change even though the planner and receipt writer require full review. Direct evaluation of the same ten-line `src/auth.ts` input returned full with `SCOPE_AUTH=true` and light with the queue's input shape. Derive these scope signals from the target commit's paths during queue verification, rather than silently omitting them or running a detector against the controller's unrelated checkout.

carry --head <sha> with no --pregate never checks that the checkout is at <sha>, but receiptDepthAtHead runs gstack-diff-scope and gstack-gate-diff on the checked-out working tree and records gate_scan.head=<sha>. A scan of another tree is then bound to the carried head, and the queue trusts it (receiptDepthVerdict), so a head with a test.skip can keep a light receipt. write refuses this case (RECEIPT_INVALID); carry does not, and no test covers it.
fix: In cmdCarry, refuse when --head is not the checked-out HEAD before computing the depth (the same guard write uses), and add a negative-path test.
test_stub: test('carry --head of a commit other than HEAD refuses and leaves the receipt', () => { /* write receipt at A; commit B with test.skip; checkout A; run carry --head B; expect EXIT.refused and receiptIn(body).head === A */ });

summary: train build (admitSlots) and ready now refuse with QUEUE_RECEIPT_DEPTH_RAISED / QUEUE_RECEIPT_EXCEPTION_INVALID and print the extra REVIEW_DEPTH line, but tests call only bindShippedReceipt directly. No test covers the refusal output or the remote base ref (refs/remotes/<remote>/<base>) that train passes.
fix: Add one ship-queue ready and one train build case with a receipt below the required depth, asserting the code and the REVIEW_DEPTH line.
test_stub: test('train build refuses a light receipt on a standard head', () => { /* seat PR whose receipt depth=light, 80 runtime lines; expect QUEUE_RECEIPT_DEPTH_RAISED and a REVIEW_DEPTH: receipt=light required=standard line */ });

summary: Light is raised to standard by fixedBlocking, blockingOpen or criticalFound. Only fixedBlocking has a test, so the blocking-open and critical-found raises and their history: reasons are uncovered.
fix: Add rows to the existing raise test for blockingOpen and criticalFound.

summary: Stale SKIP label in the new light-depth branch: on a later full pass (fullPasses > 0) of a diff that does publish numeric claims whose fingerprint is unchanged, the <reader> is skipped but the SKIP line says 'no numeric claims', which is false. The old code printed 'run once per invocation' for this case, so readers of the plan now get a wrong reason.
fix: Branch the skip text: when i.numbers.publishes is true, push '<reader> (run once per invocation; numbers unchanged)'; keep 'no numeric claims' only when !i.numbers.publishes.
test_stub: test('light pass 2 with unchanged numbers does not claim no numeric claims', () => { const p = planReview({ paths: ['lib/x.ts'], perPath: [{ path: 'lib/x.ts', lines: 5, binary: false }], scope: {}, gateTagged: 0, diffLines: 5, numbers: { publishes: true, claims: 1, fingerprint: 'f' }, reviewedNumbers: 'f', adversarialRan: true, history: { fullPasses: 1, last: 'full', fixedBelow: true } }); expect(p.skipped.join(' ')).not.toContain('no numeric claims'); });

summary: The write help says review_depth comes from 'gstack-review-plan --json at HEAD' and that 'no plan means nothing written', and the lib/ship-receipt-depth.ts header (line 7) also says it comes from gstack-review-plan. The code does neither. cmdWrite calls receiptDepthAtHead, which uses collectCommit (committed objects only, unlike the plan's collectLive working-tree view) and always returns a record: errors fail it closed to full and never stop the write.
fix: Change both texts to say the depth is recomputed from git objects at HEAD by receiptDepthAtHead (the way the queue recomputes it), with collector errors recorded as full, and remove 'no plan means nothing written'.

summary: Changed paths now come from git -z output (lib/review-collect.ts:63, ls-files -z, core.quotePath=false), so a path can hold a raw newline. The old non -z reads C-quoted control characters. diffCommand() shell-quotes each excluded docs or test path but does not strip newlines, and bin/gstack-review-plan:120 prints it on one line of a line-oriented protocol. A PR that adds a docs-class file whose name contains a newline can split DIFF_CMD:/DISPATCH: output and add forged DIFF_CMD:/DIFF_EXCLUDE: lines. The orchestrator copies those lines verbatim into reviewer prompts, so a reviewer's diff can be made to exclude real code paths.
fix: Fail the depth closed to full, or drop exclusion for any path containing control characters (/[\x00-\x1f\x7f]/) before it reaches excludeSpec/diffCommand. Sanitize paths printed in REVIEW_CLASS reasons too.

summary: Every regen check that is fresh and has a touched output now runs the generator command a second time, after deleting those outputs, to fill `proven`. lib/pregate/checks/regen.ts:26 always passes prove=ctx.touched, so each pregate on a PR that touches a generated output (for example a regenerated SKILL.md) pays a second full synchronous generator run. That can double the regen preflight time. Only `gstack-ship-receipt carry --pregate` (verifiedOutputs) reads the result, and carry is the rare path.
fix: Run the proof only when a caller asks for it: add an opt-in pregate flag that carry or /ship sets after a base merge, or run the proof lazily inside carry. Otherwise, delete all probed outputs and fold the proof into the first run, so a fresh entry costs one generator run.
evidence: lib/regen.ts:261-266 deletes the probe outputs and calls runCommand(cwd, e.command, ...) again after the verdict run at line 247; lib/pregate/checks/regen.ts:26 passes prove: ctx.touched.map(t => t.path) unconditionally

summary: Collected.mergeBase is set on all four return paths of collectCommit and collectLive, but nothing reads it: gstack-review-plan, ship-receipt-depth, the tests and the --json output never use it
fix: remove the mergeBase field from Collected and from the four result(...) calls, and keep the local mergeBase variables they already use

summary: Raising a light step to standard drops the security checklist, which breaks the invariant in docs/review-policy.md:157-159 ('a raise never dispatches less than light did'). Light's <reader> specialist always reads LIGHT_FIXED (testing, maintainability, security). The raised standard step calls specialistsFor with diffLines=50, and security there needs SCOPE_AUTH or backend >100 lines. Checked with planReview: lib/foo.ts with 30 lines and SCOPE_BACKEND gives pass 1 <reader>[testing,maintainability,security,performance,<reader>]. The same input with fixedBlocking, or with criticalFound, gives testing, maintainability, performance and <reader>, with no security. So the security checklist drops out on the pass that reviews a blocker fix.
fix: When the step is raised, include every LIGHT_FIXED specialist, for example by adding them to force for that step, and add a test that a raised step's specialists are a superset of light's checklists.

summary: The receipt's review_depth is not what the review ran. write (bin/gstack-ship-receipt:208) recomputes the depth the head needs with the same depthOfCommitInput function the queue uses, and never reads the plan's stepDepth or the review-loop rows. So QUEUE_RECEIPT_DEPTH_RAISED cannot catch a review that ran below the head's need. Example: pass 1 plans light at 40 runtime lines, fix commits push HEAD to 70, write records standard, and the queue accepts it although only light ran. The refusal text 'was reviewed at X depth' is then false. This is the gate consequence of the maintainability finding about the help text.
fix: Record the deepest depth actually dispatched (from gstack-review-plan or the review-loop rows) separately from the head's required depth. Have write refuse, and the queue check, when the dispatched depth is below the required depth.

summary: write rejects a --head other than HEAD but never checks for a dirty tree. gstack-gate-diff scans from the merge base to the working tree plus untracked files, while the depth is computed from committed objects. An uncommitted edit that reverts a committed gate-tagged hunk records gate_scan {tagged:0, head:HEAD}, and receiptDepthVerdict trusts that because it names the head. The testing specialist's carry fix (check the checkout matches --head) does not cover this, and carry already refuses dirty trees.
fix: In cmdWrite, refuse a dirty tree (git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all) with RECEIPT_INVALID, or run the gate scan in a clean worktree at head.

summary: [HIGH] [FIXABLE] lib/review-depth.ts:99, :132, :306 — any path that matches an output glob in the base registry is left out of runtime lines and out of every specialist's diff, even when the generator never writes it. isOutput is a glob match only. The base .gstack/generated.json registers "*/SKILL.md" and "*/sections/*.md" (plus runtime code such as lib/dom-dump.js and bin/gstack-doctor-components.sh). summary: [MEDIUM] [FIXABLE] lib/ship-receipt-depth.ts:42-58, called from bin/gstack-ship-receipt:208 (write) and :603 (carry) — the gate scan and scope come from the working tree but are recorded as bound to `head`. By their own headers, gstack-gate-diff and gstack-diff-scope read merge-base -> working tree plus untracked files. receiptDepthAtHead runs both in the checkout and stores gate_scan: { tagged, head }. write checks that --head is HEAD but never checks that the tree is clean (the porcelain check exists only in carry, :531). carry checks cleanliness but accepts --head <sha> that differs from the checkout when no --pregate is given, because the HEAD-equality check sits inside the pregate branch. summary: [MEDIUM] [FIXABLE (b, c) / INVESTIGATE (a)] lib/ship-receipt-depth.ts:121, :124-125 — the queue-side depth check rests on fields of the PR body it is meant to police. (a) A receipt that has neither review_depth nor gstack_version is accepted as legacy. Deleting those two keys from the body skips QUEUE_RECEIPT_DEPTH_RAISED completely, and the new test does exactly this. (b) The gate scan counts as bound when head.startsWith(rd.gate_scan.head). Use strict equality with a full sha, since write always records the full sha. (c) receiptDepthVerdict recomputes without gstack-diff-scope, so the SCOPE_AUTH and SCOPE_MIGRATIONS raises to gate are never recomputed. Verified: a 10-line lib/auth/login.ts change needs light without scope and full with SCOPE_AUTH=true. The queue's "required" depth is therefore weaker than the depth write computes.

summary: [MEDIUM] [INVESTIGATE] bin/gstack-ship-receipt:208 and lib/ship-receipt-depth.ts — review_depth records the depth the final head needs, recomputed at write time, not the depth the review actually ran. QUEUE_RECEIPT_DEPTH_RAISED compares one computation with another computation of the same function, so an honestly written receipt fails it only when rules drift. The concrete case: pass 1 plans light at 45 runtime lines. Fixes below the blocking floor push the head to 60 lines. Only fixed-blocking, blocking-open or critical-found raise the depth (planReview's raise), so no standard pass runs. write then records "standard" for the head, and the queue accepts a standard review that never happened. Fix: have write take the executed plan's depth (the REVIEW_DEPTH/step depth /ship already saves per item 6, maxed over passes) and refuse when it is below receiptDepthAtHead's.

label: High
summary: High — `carry --head` binds a gate scan to a commit it never scanned (`bin/gstack-ship-receipt:601–605`, `lib/ship-receipt-depth.ts:45–58`). `carry` accepts a target other than the checked-out HEAD, but `receiptDepthAtHead` collects that target's paths while running `gstack-diff-scope` and `gstack-gate-diff` against the current checkout. It then labels the resulting scan with the supplied target SHA. The checkout/target equality check only runs when `--pregate` is supplied. A supported failure path is a light receipt without a pregate, followed by a descendant commit that changes an ordinary test to `test.skip`. Leave the clean checkout at the reviewed commit and run `carry --head <descendant>`. The product patch is unchanged, the current checkout's scan reports no skipped test, and the carry records light depth with `gate_scan.head` set to the descendant. READY/train admission then trusts that mislabeled scan (`lib/ship-receipt-depth.ts:123–129`), so the test-skipping commit avoids the full review this change explicitly requires. No receipt tampering is necessary. Require the carried target to equal the checked-out HEAD regardless of pregate presence, or run both scope and gate scanning against the exact target's git objects before binding the scan.
